deep.reconstruction:
Folio 198r is a sheet of discarded pencil drafts, almost all struck through, plus a few ink annotations. It contains no complete derivation. What can be said with confidence:

(a) Top: two small scribbles and a closed pencil curve shaped like a kidney or heart, with an inward cusp/notch at the top. It looks like a schematic plane region or Riemann-surface sheet whose boundary curve is being studied.

(b) Struck-through lines read roughly: 'Ein Maximum oder Minimum ... gehen ...' (a maximum or minimum ... go ...), 'Rotation gerichtet' (rotation directed). A replacement phrase 'an die Begrenzungscurve' (to the boundary curve) is inserted above.

(c) Surviving line: 'Maximum ... gegen die Begrenzungscurve ... gegen das ...', with marginal letters b, c and a ∂-like sign. A struck 'Minimum' follows.

(d) A displayed relation, apparently '∂a = b − c' (the first symbol is uncertain: either ∂ or a stylised a).

(e) Lower block, mostly struck: 'Bei zweien Elementarformen ... einander ... Entwicklung' (with two elementary forms ... each other ... expansion). Surviving text: '... zweiten Form, also ein Coefficient ... ist, und einander Entwicklung' (... second form, hence a coefficient ... is, and expansion of each other).

(f) Ink annotations, written sideways: 'Laplace Mécanique céleste' (a bibliographic reminder) and 'Riemann, Dr. ph. / Correspondent d. ... Reg...' (a title or address trial, possibly connected with Riemann's corresponding membership of a learned society).

Most plausible reading (my interpretation, not certain): Riemann was sketching a counting argument for the critical points of a function on a bounded plane region. It relates the number of maxima and minima to the rotation (winding) of the gradient direction along the boundary curve. This is the kind of topological count he used in connection with Dirichlet-principle / Riemann-surface arguments.

Under that reading, '∂a = b − c' would be a bookkeeping relation between counts, e.g. change of index or rotation = (number of one type of point) − (number of another). Alternatively it is a boundary relation: the boundary of a region a equals curve b minus curve c. The fragment 'zweite Form ... Coefficient ... Entwicklung' suggests comparing two local normal forms (elementary forms) of a function near a point via series expansion. That could mean classifying a critical point by the second-order term of the expansion.

None of this is carried to a stated result. The next page (Thesen zur Optik) is unrelated; it is the draft of theses for his doctorate/habilitation, which fits the 'Dr. phil.' trial signature.
errors: No derivation is complete enough to check. The relation '∂a = b − c' is stated without defined symbols, so its correctness cannot be assessed.
The interpretation as a critical-point / boundary-rotation count is conjectural, given the heavy strike-throughs.

results.what: Apparent sketch relating maxima/minima of a function in a bounded region to the rotation along the boundary curve (Begrenzungscurve)
results.modern_name: Index/rotation counting of critical points (Kronecker index, Poincaré–Hopf, Morse-type counting on a disk)
results.usually_credited_to: Kronecker (1869), Poincaré (1885), Hopf (1926), Morse (1920s); Riemann himself used such counts for Riemann surfaces (1857)

results.modern_name: Boundary relation or difference of counts (undetermined)

results.what: Comparison of two 'Elementarformen' via coefficients of an expansion
results.modern_name: Local normal form / Taylor coefficient comparison

deep.surprise_reason: Fragmentary, mostly cancelled draft notes. The plausible topic (counting extrema via the boundary) is the kind of topological argument Riemann is already known to have used, and nothing is stated precisely enough to constitute a new result. The rest is a bibliographic note (Laplace) and a signature trial.

checkable.asserts: Illustrative example (mine): critical points are (-1,0),(1,0) (maxima) and (0,0) (saddle).

Hessian determinants are positive at the maxima and negative at the saddle, so maxima − saddles = 2 − 1 = 1. This matches index sum 1 for a region whose boundary rotation is one full turn (an illustration of the count the page appears to concern).

The right-margin ink note reads more like 'Riemann, Dr. ph.' / 'Correspondent d. Reg...' (or similar); 'Reg. Soc.' is uncertain.
Isolated marginal symbols 'b' (upper right) and a '∂'-like sign (right) are separate marks, not part of the main line.
The line 'Maximum ... gegen die Begrenzungscurve' appears to have a sign or symbol after 'Maximum', which may be a mathematical symbol rather than a word.
